findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - an Alembic upgrade uses batch operations.
The receiver check accepts only the literal name `op`. Consequently, `with op.batch_alter_table('project') as batch_op:` followed by `batch_op.drop_column('legacy_name')` or `batch_op.alter_column('status', type_=sa.Text())` produces no problems and passes close without a Contract comment. These are supported [Alembic operations](https://alembic.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/batch.html), including on Postgres. This leaves item 1 unmet. The named proof exercises only direct `op` calls, so it misses this bypass.

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 4
Case: normal use - an adopted app stores migrations at `prisma/migrations/<timestamp>/migration.sql`.
The leading `**/` requires an additional path component here: [PurePath.match treats `**` as a nonrecursive wildcard](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.PurePath.match). A root-level Prisma migration therefore fails this match and is skipped, even when it contains `DROP TABLE`. The proof uses only `apps/api/prisma/...` paths. Match the `prisma/migrations/*/migration.sql` suffix without requiring a parent directory.
